proposedSections.title: A historical constitution and its two dates
proposedSections.text: The 1939 government printing identifies Alabama and Quassarte No. 1 as former towns within Alabama-Quassarte Tribal Town. Its purposes include land, economic cooperation, health, welfare and continuing traditions. The Interior approval block is dated November 17, 1938; certification separately records ratification on January 10, 1939. Article IX protects existing rights as citizens of the Creek Nation. These are historical provisions, not an independent statement of present citizenship, leadership or governing law.

proposedSections.title: Reading the Oklahoma community's own history
proposedSections.text: An undated community account distinguishes Alabama and Quassarte towns while describing their Muscogee relationships. It presents southwestern migration and removal to Indian Territory as different historical paths, and describes traditional government continuing through federal changes. Read this as a particular Oklahoma community's interpretation, alongside primary records. Its account does not make the Oklahoma and Texas governments interchangeable; claims about present membership or administration require separately dated evidence.
